title: Leap Year Count

examples.explanation: 1996, 2000 and 2004 are leap years. 1900 is divisible by 100 but not by 400, so it isn't. 2000 is divisible by 400, so it is.

hints: First write the rule for one year: divisible by 4, except years divisible by 100, except years divisible by 400.
Ranges go up to 10¹⁸ years, so you can't loop over them. How many multiples of 4 are there from 1 to y?
Let f(y) count leap years in 1..y. Then f(y) = ⌊y/4⌋ − ⌊y/100⌋ + ⌊y/400⌋, and the answer for [L, R] is f(R) − f(L − 1).
